prerequisites: No prior knowledge is required beyond what is expected at the beginning of a university stage and, in any case, an open and favorable attitude towards permanent and self-directed learning.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the relationships between the subsystems of the company.
Understand the concept of the management process and the functions that comprise it.
Understand the different criteria that can be used to classify organizations into different groups.
Understand the function of the production subsystem and how to achieve the efficiency of the subsystem.
Understand the basic financial statements of the company and their interpretation.
Understand the main functions that human resources managers must carry out to ensure the success and long-term survival of the company.
Understand the principles, basic concepts, and nature of Marketing.
Produce a grammatically correct, well-structured, clear, content-rich, and situationally appropriate written text.
Organize and participate in work teams, fostering aptitudes for empathy, negotiation, and the optimization of time and personnel involved.
Effectively present and explain individual or group work in a debate environment to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Function effectively in a team whose members together provide leadership and create a collaborative and inclusive environment in the organization and coordination of work.
Collaborate proactively in the development of work, establishing goals and meeting objectives.
Contribute to the search for solutions to challenges or projects, demonstrating empathy and assertiveness when sharing ideas, reflections and arguments within collaborative work.
Demonstrate initiative to organize one's own work, managing effort and time dedicated to achieving the proposed objectives and goals.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. The company and business management
The company as an open system
The functional subsystems of the company
Topic 2. Ownership, management and governance of the company
Concept of ownership, management and governance of the company
Topic 3. Evolution of the main Schools of Administration and Organization
Traditional Schools of Organization: classical approaches
Classification of organizations: criteria and application
Strategic decisions on the product or service
Strategic decisions on the production process
Strategic decisions on capacity and location of facilities
New technologies in the production process. The Just in Time System.
teaching_methods: Expositive lectures (participatory master class, conferences, company visits, trade fair attendance)
Participatory classes (individual or group problem-solving, role-playing, application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates)
Tutorials (personalized and small group attention, review, re-guidance of materials, consultation)

assessment_methods.method: Individual written knowledge tests (objective tests, development, short answers, problems, comments, assessments)
Written tests through reports/memoirs and presentation of team and individual work on specific subject content

assessment_rules: For the first attempt, the final grade is calculated as 25% Integrated Project + 30% Continuous Assessment + 45% Knowledge Test. A minimum of 40% of the weight assigned to the knowledge test criterion must be obtained to pass the subject. For the second attempt, students can choose to keep the grades for the Integrated Project and Continuous Assessment (Option 1), in which case the knowledge test will account for 45% of the final grade, and a minimum of 40% in this test is required. Alternatively, students can waive both the Integrated Project and Continuous Assessment grades (Option 2), making the knowledge test account for 100% of the final grade. The use of AI tools is permitted with citation (Level 2) or with full traceability (Level 3), otherwise it may be considered plagiarism, except for in-person tests where no AI use is allowed (Level 1).
